episodes.159395: Several waterspouts were reported over the Chesapeake Bay in the morning, with localized gusty winds over the upper tidal Potomac River in the evening.
episodes.159475: There was a marine thunderstorm wind gust in Galveston Bay.
episodes.159478: A waterspout moved onshore along the Bolivar Peninsula.
episodes.159488: Slow moving afternoon storms near a stalled frontal boundary resulted in flash flooding.
episodes.159520: Some marine thunderstorm winds were observed.
episodes.159527: Evening thunderstorms that moved over the Cape in Brevard County produced strong wind gusts.
episodes.159533: Numerous afternoon thunderstorms developed along the sea breeze collision and moved toward the coast. A few storms became severe, with one producing a waterspout in New Smyrna Beach, and others producing many strong wind gusts in Brevard County.
episodes.159534: A couple of severe thunderstorms developed along the sea breeze collision. One storm produced a tornado in New Smyrna Beach, and another produced wind damage in Saint Cloud.
episodes.159714: Abundant monsoon moisture remained in place across the Western Slope. This, paired with increased instability, resulted in another round of showers and thunderstorms with the stronger storms producing heavy rain. This led to a debris flow in Garfield County within the Pine Gulch Fire burn scar.
episodes.159715: Abundant monsoon moisture remained in place across eastern Utah. This, paired with increased instability, resulted in another round of showers and thunderstorms with the stronger storms producing heavy rain. Flooding and debris flows occurred with several storms including on the Pack Creek Fire burn scar.
episodes.159773: Abundant monsoon moisture across southwest Colorado resulted in another round of showers and thunderstorms. Some storms produced heavy rain which led to localized debris flows in San Juan County.
episodes.160270: Anomalously high precipitable water values worked their way into Southwestern Montana, along with weak upper level flow. This combination resulted in slow moving heavy thunderstorms, which produced some impressive rainfall totals in places. For example, a meson site reported over 1.6 of rain, with 1.36 of that falling in just 20 minutes. This lead to some urban flash flooding, with a report out of Bozeman, MT of water flowing swiftly from south to north in the downtown area.
episodes.161116: SW flow focused afternoon and evening sea breeze storms toward the Atlantic coast. A weak surface front was draped across NE FL which aided in convergence.
episodes.161117: A strong short wave tracked across the area from the west during the afternoon and evening hours. This feature combined with a moist and very unstable low level airmass produced strong storms along sea breezes and outflow boundaries that produced heavy rainfall and gusty winds.
episodes.161118: A strong short wave tracked across the area from the west during the afternoon and evening hours. This feature combined with a moist and very unstable low level airmass produced strong storms along sea breezes and outflow boundaries that produced heavy rainfall and gusty winds.
episodes.161632: A Tropical Upper Tropospheric Trough near the area and near normal moisture values combined with strong daytime heating and local effects to generate shower and thunderstorm activity across the San Juan metro as well as western and northwestern portions of Puerto Rico.
episodes.161634: A Tropical Upper Tropospheric Trough (TUTT) and near normal moisture combined with daytime heating and local effects to generate a line of heavy showers, affecting the San Juan metro area.
episodes.161746: An upper level disturbance and developing area of low pressure allowed for scattered showers and thunderstorms to develop on the night of August 1st.  These storms developed in a moisture rich atmosphere which allowed for heavy rainfall rates within the stronger storms.  The heaviest rainfall occurred in Sullivan County where amounts of 2.5 to 3��� of rain were reported.  Lighter amounts of 1 to 2��� were reported in surrounding counties.  The combination of the record wet July and heavy rainfall on this night led to excessive run-off and localized flash flooding across Sullivan County. River response on the preceding days kept area rivers near all time high flows for the calendar date, but all rivers remained below flood stage with no significant impacts.
episodes.161766: Monsoonal subtropical moisture set the stage for thunderstorms to produce heavy rainfall across southwest Montana. North of this moisture plume, the Boulder 2700 fire burned down structures near Montana Highway 35 along the southeastern shore of Flathead Lake.
episodes.161771: Monsoonal subtropical moisture set the stage for thunderstorms to produce heavy rainfall across portions of the central Idaho.
episodes.161775: A strong thunderstorm produced excessive rainfall over Big Sky Lake during the afternoon of August 2nd.
episodes.161905: Continued push of monsoonal moisture into Idaho caused continued flooding into the first couple of days of August.
episodes.162008: An environment marked by warm and moist conditions favored strong to severe thunderstorms while an outflow boundary collided with a sea breeze circulation under mid-level energy traversing across the region.
episodes.162009: An environment marked by warm and moist conditions favored strong to severe thunderstorms while an outflow boundary collided with a sea breeze circulation under mid-level energy traversing across the region.
episodes.162210: A waterspout was reported over Sabine Lake from an isolated developing thunderstorm.
episodes.162223: Daytime heating combined with abundant moisture allowed for isolated convection to develop over favored terrain features in southern Gila County during the afternoon and evening on the 1st. Thunderstorms were capable of producing locally heavy rainfall, which ended up resulting in one instance of flash flooding. A USGS stream gage along Cibecue Creek recorded a rapid rise of 4 feet in less than 15 minutes. No damage or injuries were reported.
episodes.162270: A cold front moved into a warm, moist airmass and generated thunderstorms over South Central Texas. Some of these storms produced locally heavy rain that led to flash flooding.
episodes.162345: Increasing surface moisture and shortwave trough embedded in southwest flow aloft lead to the initiation of convection across portions of central OR in the early afternoon. The storms were strong enough to produce hail around an inch across Deschutes and Crook counties.
episodes.162439: Slow moving thunderstorms developed over the mountains, as the monsoon plume remained in place on this day. With the heavy rain that stemmed from these thunderstorms along with high antecedent soil moistures from rainfall over the past several days, the flash flood threat remained high with a few reports of flash flooding noted near the higher terrain.
episodes.162464: Moist and unstable southwest wind flow combined with a locally unstable atmosphere to produce strong showers and thunderstorms over SE Florida and the adjacent Atlantic waters.
episodes.162465: Moist and unstable southwest wind flow combined with a locally unstable atmosphere to produce strong showers and thunderstorms over SE Florida and the adjacent Atlantic waters.
episodes.162506: An upper level disturbance enhanced convective activity along a stalled out cold front near the I-85 corridor. The storms produced periods very heavy rainfall, damaging winds, and frequent lightning across Montgomery County.
episodes.162616: An active monsoon surge brought thunderstorms producing heavy rain, damaging wind gusts, and hail across the state.
episodes.162629: Deep moisture over northern Arizona lead to scattered thunderstorms with heavy rain that caused flash flooding.
episodes.162789: Monsoonal moisture associated with a low pressure system brought locally heavy rain and thunderstorms to southwestern Oregon and southeastern Idaho. Flash flood watches were issued to the area due to the extensive precipitation.
episodes.162851: A weak disturbance moving through northwest flow aloft triggered a few isolated thunderstorms over far southwest New Mexico with one storm producing a severe wind gust over the Lordsburg Playa.

Mud, rocks and other debris flowed across La Sal Pass Road as a result of heavy rain over the Pack Creek Fire burn scar.

Several lane on Interstate 15 near Bountiful were closed due to standing water. Hill Field Road near Hill Air Force Base was flooded.  Basement flooding occurred in Centerville.

A video showed a significant rise of water flowing through the wash.

Water, mud and debris flow from the Pack Creek Fire burn scar reached Spanish Valley as far north as the intersection of Beeman Road and Spanish Valley Road. The culverts were not big enough to hold water. Water, mud and debris went over the road and came into some basements a couple inches deep.
Idaho Transportation Department reported water running across Idaho Highwy 37 between Lawery Lane and Cow Canyon Road.

A USGS stream gage along Cibecue Creek near Chrysotile, Arizona recorded a rapid rise of over 4 feet in less than 15 minutes. At 2205MST, the creek crested at 6.9 feet. No damage or injuries were reported.

Flash flooding in Charlestown caused a road washouts, one on Route 12 between Almar St and Bowen Crossing. Another washout occurred on Scenic Hill Rd at Wheeler Rand Rd. The washouts were the result of overland runoff and not from any river or creek.  At least six roads were closed in Charlestown, Pecor Road, Lamb Road, Meany Road, South Hemlock and Hackett Swamp. Nearby rain gages reported between 1.88-2.57 between 730 PM and midnight.

Heavy rainfall across southern and central New Hampshire on August 1 caused flash flooding due to already saturated ground conditions from a record wet July. In West Unity, a weather observer measured at 2.57 between 730 PM and midnight. Rapid runoff caused several roads to sustain damage such as undermining of pavement to a complete washout. West Unity Road was the hardest hit with a large sinkhole estimated at 10 feet.

A significant flood wave carrying debris moved down Bear Creek Canyon, sweeping away mining vehicles at the Gentry Mountain Mine. Several miners were caught in the flood waters, with one miner able to save himself by clinging to a tree a quarter mile down the drainage. Another miner was not able to escape the flood waters and was found deceased 6 miles downstream. Another Mine car was flipped 8 times in the flood waters, but the miners were able to kick out the windows and escape. Significant infrastructure damage occurred at the Mine.

Based on information provided by the Volusia County Sheriffs Office, a short-lived tornado touched down just west of U.S. Highway 1, near the intersection of Sleepy Hollow Road, in New Smyrna Beach. Peak winds are estimated around 55-65 mph. The tornado touched down at approximately 1340LST, then traveled half of a mile east where it became a waterspout over the Intracoastal Waterway. The waterspout dissipated around 1341LST before reaching the barrier island. The tornado produced tree damage along Sleepy Hollow Road that included several medium to large-sized branches downed, and a couple of small trees knocked over. No additional damage reports were received.
